or-01-pai-nosso.context: The disciples see Jesus pray and want to learn. Instead of a magic formula, Jesus gives them a short prayer that begins with the Father and the kingdom, before any need of theirs.
or-01-pai-nosso.focusQuestion: How would your prayers change if they began with the kingdom, not with hurry?
or-01-pai-nosso.keywordGloss: Jesus' prayer begins by calling God Father, and our Father: everyone's, not only mine.
facts: The prayer begins with the Father who is in heaven and his name hallowed.
It asks that the kingdom come and that God's will be done on earth as in heaven.
The bread asked for is each day's, given today.
Forgiveness is asked as we have forgiven our debtors.
It asks not to fall into temptation, but to be delivered from evil.
The prayer closes declaring that the kingdom, power, and glory are God's forever.

or-02-persistencia.context: Jesus tells this parable with a stated aim right at the opening: to teach that one must pray always and never lose heart. The central character is a widow with no power at all before a judge who respects no one.
or-02-persistencia.focusQuestion: What petition did you give up on too soon and need to bring back to God?
or-02-persistencia.keywordGloss: Pray always and never lose heart: return to God again, trusting that he is just.
reflectionPrompts: God is not the unjust judge
facts: The parable was told about the need to pray always and never lose heart.
The judge in the story neither feared God nor respected any person.
The widow asked him to judge her case against her adversary.
The judge answered because of the widow's insistence.
God will do justice for his chosen ones, who cry to him day and night.
Jesus promises justice quickly and asks whether he will find faith on the earth.

or-03-espirito.context: Paul speaks of a world that groans and of believers who suffer without even knowing how to ask. It is at that point of weakness, not of strength, that the Holy Spirit's help in prayer enters.
or-03-espirito.focusQuestion: What would you do in prayer if you knew you did not need to get the words right?
or-03-espirito.keywordGloss: When we do not know how to pray as we ought, the Spirit himself intercedes for us, according to God's will.
facts: The Spirit helps us in our weaknesses.
We do not know how to pray as we ought.
The Spirit himself intercedes for us with inexpressible groans.
The one who searches the hearts knows the Spirit's purpose.
He intercedes for the saints according to God's will.

or-04-desafio.context: This challenge joins the three teachings of the trail: Jesus teaches to pray to the Father beginning with the kingdom, the parable says to persist without losing heart, and Paul shows the Spirit interceding in our weakness.
or-04-desafio.focusQuestion: Which of the three helps — form, persistence, or Spirit — do you need most today?
or-04-desafio.keywordGloss: Pray as children, keep going without losing heart, and count on the Spirit when words fail.
reflectionPrompts: Without losing heart in the wait
facts: Jesus' prayer begins with the Father and his name hallowed.
The bread asked for in the Lord's Prayer is each day's.
The parable was told so we would pray always and never lose heart.
God will do justice for his chosen ones, who cry day and night.
The Spirit helps us in our weaknesses when we pray.
He intercedes for the saints according to God's will.
